q1_can_any_smooth_spacetime_be_trivially.answer: No. The bare-metric class is not vacuous, and the extension predicate is strong enough to make the question substantive.
q1_can_any_smooth_spacetime_be_trivially.argument_from_exact_definition: The predicate at lines 96-103 requires (a) an isometric embedding, (b) onto an open PROPER subset of a connected time-orientable M', (d) with continuous nondegenerate Lorentzian g', (e) no equation required, and (f) added points lying to the future of the image. Those clauses are not automatic.
q1_can_any_smooth_spacetime_be_trivially.non_vacuity_witness: Minkowski spacetime (the E=0 datum) satisfies the class conclusion: assume a proper future C0 extension exists; take a g'-timelike curve from q in iota(M) to p outside iota(M). Under the standard locally-Lipschitz causal-curve convention the segment inside iota(M) from q to the first exit point r has finite eta-length, so it stays in the compact eta-timelike determination K = {x : tau(q,x) >= 0, |x-q| <= L}; iota(K) is compact hence closed in M', so r lies in iota(K) subset iota(M), contradicting r on the boundary. Hence no such extension exists and the class has a satisfiable conclusion.
q1_can_any_smooth_spacetime_be_trivially.non_triviality_of_falsification: Conversely exact subextremal Kerr data admit a smooth (hence C0) proper extension (line 258), so the conclusion fails there; the Dafermos-Luk anchor (provenance) conditionally makes the failure generic. The class therefore has both positive and negative instances: vacuity is refuted in both directions.
q1_can_any_smooth_spacetime_be_trivially.caveat_on_my_argument: This is the reviewer's elementary argument, not a cited theorem. It respects the schema's own c0_uniqueness_caveat (lines 113-117): it does not use geodesic uniqueness or g'-completeness; it uses only the flat metric inside iota(M) and continuity of g'. It does assume the standard convention that causal curves are locally Lipschitz so that length is defined on compact parameter intervals.
q1_can_any_smooth_spacetime_be_trivially.residual_defect: non_vacuity.condition (lines 221-225) is a caveat on applications, not part of the formal statement (line 253). Applied to a development with a smoothly attachable boundary, the formal statement can be trivially false. Recommend stating explicitly that genericity is what excludes smoothly extendible data, or add the condition to the class's application rule.
q1_can_any_smooth_spacetime_be_trivially.scope_caveat: The witness refutes vacuity of the extension predicate and of the class as a statement about AF vacuum developments. If the frozen generic set G excludes the Minkowski point (the F2a sibling's ADM decision excludes E=0), Minkowski does not witness non-vacuity of the generic class statement; that then rests on the schema's trapped-surface family in G, which the schema marks UNVERIFIED at line 227. The answer to 'is the bare-metric class vacuous' is therefore no at the predicate level, and conditionally no at the generic-statement level.

q2_is_a_disjunctive_d0_domain_acceptable.answer: No. A disjunction of regularity settings makes the comeagre quantifier topology-relative and turns one class into a family of statements.
q2_is_a_disjunctive_d0_domain_acceptable.reason: Comeagreness is defined in a named topology. A union of two completions (smooth-with-decay and weighted Sobolev) has no single topology unless one is declared the ambient space; the quantifier 'exists comeagre G' then has different meanings in the two readings, so the artifact is not one class statement.
q2_is_a_disjunctive_d0_domain_acceptable.state_of_this_revision: PASS internally: revision 6 removes the disjunction. Lines 71-74 define a single Frechet topology and a single data class; lines 160-167 freeze smooth-with-decay and mark the Sobolev setting explicitly as not-this-class, not quantified over; line 273 forbids reintroducing a disjunctive domain; line 318 lists the Sobolev variant in anti_scope. The single_class_note at line 87 is now accurate.
q2_is_a_disjunctive_d0_domain_acceptable.cross_artifact_consequence: The portfolio still has two data classes: F1 and F2a currently freeze weighted Sobolev H^4_{1/2+epsilon}, F2b freezes smooth-with-decay. That is acceptable for F2b in isolation but blocks G-FORM's one-data-class criterion; the freeze decision belongs to lead-formulation. Note the F2a sibling still carries a disjunctive residue in its statement_formal (see reviews/F2a-review-18.json HF-A2).

q3_are_tier_1_tier_2_falsifiers_correctl.answer: Yes in structure; no in the machine-checkability labelling.
q3_are_tier_1_tier_2_falsifiers_correctl.correct_part: tier_1 (lines 295-300) refutes the class and correctly requires a NON-MEAGER set of extendible data with explicit extension data, matching the negation normal form at lines 76-80. tier_2 (lines 301-304) refutes only the all-data strengthening and is labelled refutes_strengthening_only. A single Kerr-type datum therefore cannot be counted against the class.
q3_are_tier_1_tier_2_falsifiers_correctl.defect: machine_checkable_steps (line 299) labels four items machine-checkable, but only 'constraint residuals below tolerance' is. 'g-prime continuous and nondegenerate on a neighbourhood of the boundary (sampled)' is numerical evidence, not a check; 'iota is an isometry onto an open proper subset' and 'the added points lie to the future of iota(M)' are proof obligations. non_machine_checkable_step (line 300) names only non-meagerness and understates the set.
q3_are_tier_1_tier_2_falsifiers_correctl.recommendation: Split the list into (i) machine-checkable residuals, (ii) numerically checkable on an explicit finite representation, (iii) proof obligations. The same defect exists in the F2a sibling (reviews/F2a-review-18.json F-A7); this is one correlated finding across the two artifacts, not two independent ones.
